2608.04193.title: Patients-like-me: A Variational LM--GNN Framework for Explainable Clinical Prediction
2608.04193.paper_summary: Language models (LMs) offer strong textual representations for electronic health records (EHRs), but they encode patient sequences in isolation and provide limited explainability. Graph neural networks (GNNs) complement LMs by incorporating inter-patient relationships and enabling reference-patient attribution, yet they rely on high-quality patient representations. We propose Patients-like-me (PLM), a unified LM--GNN framework that integrates local patient semantics with global cohort structure. To train PLM efficiently, we introduce a Variational Expectation-Maximization algorithm that alternates LM and GNN updates under a supervised variational objective. Extensive experiments on MIMIC-III and MIMIC-IV show that PLM consistently outperforms state-of-the-art methods, with improvements generalizing across encoder-only and decoder-only LM backbones. These gains are achieved with only modest additional computational overhead. PLM also provides reference-patient explanations by retrieving influential similar patients, while edge-masking experiments confirm that the highest-ranked references have the greatest impact on model predictions.
2608.04193.paper_summary_zh: 語言模型（LMs）為電子健康記錄（EHRs）提供強大的文本表示，但它們在孤立中編碼患者序列，並提供有限的可解釋性。圖神經網絡（GNNs）通過整合患者之間的關係並實現參考患者歸因來補充LMs，但它們依賴於高質量的患者表示。我們提出了Patients-like-me（PLM），這是一個統一的LM-GNN框架，將局部患者語義與全局隊列結構相結合。為了有效地訓練PLM，我們引入了一種變分期望最大化算法，該算法在監督變分目標下交替進行LM和GNN的更新。在MIMIC-III和MIMIC-IV上的廣泛實驗顯示，PLM始終超越最先進的方法，改進在僅編碼器和僅解碼器的LM骨幹中普遍存在。這些增益僅需適度的額外計算開銷即可實現。PLM還通過檢索有影響力的相似患者來提供參考患者解釋，而邊緣遮蔽實驗證實，排名最高的參考對模型預測的影響最大。
